whisper.transcript: If you connect 200,000 living human brain cells to doom... They can help make the character shoot. Scientists actually did it. The cells aren't inside someone's head. They're growing on a chip. The game sends electrical signals into them, and when the neurons fire back, software translates their activity into commands to move, turn, and shoot. They're terrible at the game, and a normal computer still does much of the work. But the weirdest part is real. This video game controller is alive.
